tasks.short: Prepare bibliographies, charts and graphs as teaching aids

steps.what: Plan teaching aids and capture actual source metadata and chart data from the teacher's brief.
outputs: Selected citation metadata and validated chart data

steps.what: Prepare the bibliography from captured source metadata using native citation tools in {DOCS}.
inputs: Selected citation metadata and validated chart data

steps.what: Develop charts and graphs from the actual validated data using native {SPREADSHEET} charts.
inputs: Selected citation metadata and validated chart data

steps.what: Check references, axes, units and instructional meaning, repairing omissions and misleading chart choices.
Review the complete final teaching aids for lesson suitability and classroom release.
Save the ordinary final teaching aid file in its existing location.
Release the exact teacher-approved teaching aids to the class material area in {LMS}.

tasks.design: Use native citation formatting in {DOCS} and charts in {SPREADSHEET} for exact teaching-aid assembly. The assistant captures sources and data, checks every reference and visual meaning, and the teacher reviews the final version before its separate {LMS} release; no model or autonomous agent is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source selection and chart meaning are mixed with repeated formatting and drawing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing citation and chart tools can remove manual layout where actual source fields and data are available.
tasks.still_hard: A correct number can still be shown with a misleading scale or unsuitable explanation.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an aid that helps students understand the lesson rather than decorating it.

ambition.what: Offer a second visual representation of the same class dataset for teacher comparison.

tasks.altitude: Less manual bibliography/graph formatting; more source and visual-meaning checks under the teacher's direction.

reach.task: Compare two representations of one lesson dataset

evidence.claim: Native citation and chart tools can format captured bibliographic fields and validated data without inventing sources or instructional decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is actual production of bibliographies and charts/graphs under a teacher's existing brief, with actual final classroom release. Teacher review8 is other-role labour, excluded from the assistant denominator and fully retained. No research, grading or teaching saving is borrowed.

S4 retains source verification, chart-choice judgement and all failed-format repair. No free structured bibliography or clean new dataset is assumed.

Test native citation and chart tools first. S2 removes only actual citation layout, s3 only actual graph construction; substantive source/data work stays in s1/s4. Existing automatic charts/citations earn no new benefit. Ordinary save time is1 retained and ungated.

tasks.design: Keep actual paper distribution and collection human and retain the existing {LMS} return checklist. Test native assignment settings first; where the class list and checkboxes already exist, there is no further formatting or transfer to remove without changing the assessment medium and pupil access.

tasks.enabler_now: No new capability in this paper workflow removes distribution, collection or actual return capture.
tasks.still_hard: A pile of papers does not show whether a particular student's actual work is present.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve an absent name, misplaced paper or access problem without wrongly marking work missing.
tasks.altitude: No change in task time or authority to set assignments.

evidence.claim: An existing digital checklist does not eliminate collecting or checking actual paper returns.

outputs: Actual counted project cash and payer identity

Verified collection identity and expected amount

tasks.design: Configure the actual project collection worksheet in {SPREADSHEET} with the existing student list, stable project fields and an exact total. The assistant still counts cash, enters the actual amount, checks and issues each receipt, reconciles discrepancies and physically hands over the money; no payment is inferred from an expected amount.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash handling is mixed with repeated project identifiers and hand totals.
tasks.enabler_now: Native validation and sums can remove only that worksheet repetition and arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: The money actually received may differ from the requested amount or claimed payer.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve a payment question without confusing a child's circumstances with a missing payment.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated field entry and arithmetic; cash custody and payment judgement remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native worksheet fields and sums can reduce repeated identifiers and hand totals without collecting or verifying actual cash.

assumptions: Boundary is actual school-project cash collection with an existing collection worksheet and receipt practice. It does not create a new payment register or move unpaid fees to a bank integration. Custodian accounting after actual handoff is unchanged and receives no saving.

School project owner supplies approved project id and expected amount in normal project setup. S1 checks it and the actual student list; s2 counts actual cash and identifies payer; s3 manually captures actual amount/date/payer. S6 only totals those existing entries; s7 retains discrepancy and failed-formula repair. No actual payment flag is generated from a request.
